narrative:
The model estimated a 57.2% chance that you would fail the bar exam on the first try. Because that risk was high enough to fall on the failing side of the decision, your law school application was denied; this is not a certainty of failure, but the model judged the risk too high for admission.

The strongest factor was your undergraduate GPA of 3.10, slightly below the 3.23 average among accepted students. In this prediction it was the most influential feature and leaned toward passing, so it was not the main reason for denial. The next most important factor was your LSAT score of 25, well below the accepted average of 37.18; this pushed strongly toward likely bar failure. Third was your Year 3 class rank decile of 2, compared with an accepted average near 5.8, which also pushed toward failure. Together, the low LSAT and weak third-year standing outweighed the modest positive signal from your GPA.

To improve future chances, focus on raising your LSAT score if you can retake it, strengthen your academic record in advanced coursework, and seek admissions advising about delaying or reapplying. A targeted plan to address these specific weaknesses would make a later application more competitive.
